newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 ends flat as weak gilts, Dow weigh.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 ends flat as weak gilts, Dow weigh.

text.p: The FTSE 100 ended practically unchanged on Monday as profit-taking in the U.S. and in the UK gilt market deflated an early rally that had propelled UK blue chips to a record peak, dealers said.
The leading UK share index ended 0.1 point lower at 4,307.7, with advancers narrowly outpacing decliners 51 to 47.
"It's Wall Street that has got us down -- what else?" said one market-maker of the late decline.
Earlier, the FTSE 100 climbed to a record peak at 4,330.0, buoyed by another dose of bid speculation, benign inflation figures and a solid performance on Wall Street on Friday.
A smaller-than-expected 0.2 percent rise in the UK January producer output price index reinforced the view that interest rates will probably remain steady for the time being.
Continued low rates should translate into further gains in UK shares, strategists said.
"If gilts stay where they are, I think the market can go higher from here," said Tim Russell, head of UK equities at Lazard Investors Fund Management.
Yet the possibility of a sharp correction on Wall Street and of a U.S. rate rise plus continued volatility in the currency markets continue to restrain the stock market.
The Dow's near 83-point gain on Friday hoisted UK shares early on, but the rally faded as U.S. shares erased opening gains and sank on profit-taking on Monday.

British financial and insurance sectors clung on to gains as bid speculation swirled through dealing rooms in the wake of last week's announcement that U.S. investment banks Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter Discover & Co plan to merge operation.
"That merger seemed to refocus attention on the idea that there will be more consolidation in this industry," said one marketmaker.
Shares in Mercury Asset Management Plc and Schroders Plc surged to record levels after press reports that Merrill Lynch was eyeing the UK firms.
Merrill Lynch declined to comment on the talk.

And though some brokers were sceptical of the weekend press report, shares in Mercury jumped 29p to 1385 after having surged as high as 1415, while shares in added 2-1/2p to 1755, having reached a peak at 1788.
Bid speculation and bullish comments from brokerage BZW helped propelled insurance shares higher.
Shares in Prudential Corp firmed 10p to 582, off the all-time high of 592 set earlier. Shares in Legal & General added 6p to 404-1/2.
The UK bank sector rallied, with several stocks climbing to records, on expectations the sector will report strong results, dealers said.
Lloyds TSB Group rose 7p to 493-1/2, after setting a record at 507, ahead of releasing its annual results on Friday.
Elsewhere, shares in British Airways Plc jumped 11p to 597-1/2 after the air carrier delivered record third quarter
Shares in Granada Group Plc dropped 18p to 894-1/2 after the company's chairman Gerry Robinson cut his stake.
Some UK food retailers felt the pressure of a downgrade in earnings estimates for the sector by BZW.
